title: How does a robot arm become a welding cell?
scope: Industrial robots used in arc welding
lead: Follow the handoffs from a joint reducer to an accepted weld. Each supplier delivers a different capability.
figure: Four roles from joint motion to weld quality

stages.name: Component maker
stages.caption: Joint transmission
stages.detail: A precision reducer works with the motor to deliver the speed and torque a joint needs.

stages.name: Robot maker
stages.caption: Controlled motion
stages.detail: Mechanical joints, drives and a controller move the arm along a programmed path.

stages.name: System integrator
stages.caption: Welding cell
stages.detail: The integrator selects the torch, power supply, fixtures and guarding, then programs and tests the cell.

stages.name: Factory
stages.caption: Accepted parts
stages.detail: The factory checks weld quality and cycle time against its requirements and plans maintenance.

notes.title: What does the joint supply?
notes.body: A reducer transmits motion at the joint. Motor sizing, sensing and control also shape how the arm moves.

notes.title: What does integration add?
notes.body: The arm can reach a point in space. Making a repeatable weld also takes a fixture that locates the part and a torch and power source working together.

notes.title: How is value verified?
notes.body: Trial-weld a representative part, inspect the joint and time the full cycle. These checks show whether the cell meets production needs.

insight.title: What if the fixture shifts?
insight.body: The real seam can move away from the programmed path. An integrator can improve the fixture or add seam finding, then check how the extra motion affects cycle time.

boundary: These roles can overlap. Welding equipment and tooling may be supplied directly to the integrator. The diagram covers industrial arc welding.
feedback: The factory specifies part size, weld locations and cycle time. The integrator uses these to select equipment.
